raw_segments.text: Against our coast appears a spacious land, which once the fierce Lycurgus did command,
Thracia the name.
The people bowled in war, vast are their fields and tillage is their care, a hospitable realm
while fate was kind, with Troyan friendship and religion joined.
I land, with luckless omens, then adore their gods and draw a line along the shore.
I lay the deep foundations of a wall and Enos, nammed from me, the city call.
To Dene and Venus vows are paid, and all the powers that rising labors aid,
a bull on Jove's imperial altar laid.
Not far, a rising hillock stood in view, sharp myrtles on the sides and cornals grew.
There, while I went to crop the sylvan scenes and shade our altar with their leafy greens,
I pulled a plant, with horror I relayed a prodigy so strange and full of fate.
The rooted fibers rose, and from the wound black bloody drops distilled upon the ground.
Mute and amazed, my hair with terror stood, fear shrunk my sinews and congealed my blood.
Manned once again, another plant I try, that other gushed with the same sanguine dye.
Then, fearing guilt for some offense unknown, with prayers and vows the dryads I atone
with all the sisters of the woods and most the god of arms, who rules the Thracian coast,
that they or he these omens would avert, release our fears and better signs impart.
Cleared as I thought and fully fixed at length to learn the cause, I tugged with all my strength.
I bent my knees against the ground. Once more the violated myrtle ran with gore.
Scarce dare I tell the sequel, from the womb of wounded earth and caverns of the tomb,
a groan, as of a troubled ghost, renewed my fright, and then these dreadful words ensued.
Why dost thou thus my buried body rend? O spare the corpse of thy unhappy friend.
Spare to pollute thy pious hands with blood. The tears distill not from the wounded wood,
but every drop this living tree contains is kindred blood and ran in trojan veins.
O fly from this unhospitable shore, warned by my fate, for I am polador.
Hear loads of lances in my blood and brood again shoot upward by my blood renewed.
